newsitem.title: BELARUS: CIS leaders postpone Moscow summit.
newsitem.headline: CIS leaders postpone Moscow summit.

text.p: A summit meeting of leaders of the Commonwealth of Independent States will not take place on January 29 as planned, the CIS secretariat in the Belarussian capital Minsk said on Friday.
"The summit will not take place," a press spokesman said, adding that further information would be available shortly.

The secretariat said the meeting, already postponed once, had been put back to another date. It had been expected to focus on economic integration in the CIS, the loose 12-nation bloc that replaced the Soviet Union more than five years ago.
A spokesman said the presidents of Belarus, Ukraine, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan had asked Russian President Boris Yeltsin to postpone the meeting, which had been due to take place in Moscow.
"B. Yeltsin supported the suggestion of postponing the meeting," he added.
Yeltsin, 65, has been away from the Kremlin for most of the last seven months, first with heart problems and then with pneumonia. He underwent a heart bypass operation on November 5.

His illness overshadowed a meeting last Friday of CIS prime ministers in Moscow. Eight of the 12 premiers at that meeting signed draft guidelines on economic ties that were due to be discussed at the January 29 summit.
The CIS groups all the former Soviet republics except the three Baltic republics Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.
